revision.text: [[File:PlusPlus Logo.png|thumb|The logo for Plus+]] '''Plus+''' was a social gaming network created by ngmoco in 2009 for the iPhone. It closed on 31 March 2013 following the purchase of ngmoco by DeNA, who provided a similar service in eastern countries. Its infrastructure seems to have been used for DeNA's attempted entrance into the western market, '''Mobage West''', which acted as the successor to Plus+. Mobage West was reportedly shut down in 2018 with no notice given, though there is seemingly no reliable source for this. == Plus+ SDK == === Network Requests === Some network requests to the Plus+ servers at app.plusplus.com are done asynchronously by: # Creating an instance of NGPlatformAPIOperation. # Initialising with a callback of the form -(void)[object callback: (NGPlatformAPIOperationResult) result] and an object to preform it on. # Setting a few properties using setters, like user info (extra data passed to callback), the http method, the endpoint, and weather to use TLS or not. # Adding it to the request queue using the enqueue method. Note that requests are usually done asynchronously. As an example, here is a decompiled method to ping the Plus+ server: - (void) pingPlusServerWithTarget: (NSObject) target action: (SEL) action { NGPlatformAPIOperation *operation = [[NGPlatformAPIOperation alloc] initWithTarget: this action: "_pingCallback:"]; NSDictionary *user_info = [NSDictionary dictionaryWithObjectsAndKeys: target, @"target", @selector(action), @"action", nil]; [operation setUserInfo: user_info]; [operation setHttpMethod: @"GET"]; [operation setApiMethod: @"ping"]; [operation enqueue]; } Sometimes, they are also done synchronously using synchronouslyPerformAction:method:data:. Some more complicated record types are typically initialised by passing a response dictionary into an initWithDictionary: method. == Plus+ Server == === Misc Details === [[File:Screenshot 20250614 034104.png|thumb|Original headers for Plus+ server, according to archive.org. Notice the use of Phusion Passenger with Ruby on Rails.]] The original Plus+ server appears to have been written in Ruby. === Requests === Requests are sent to app.plusplus.com over HTTP (or HTTPS if the request explicitly specifies itself to be secure). Plus+ constructs the user agent from the app key and version, plus+ sdk version and OS and version: {appKey}/{appVersion} PlusPlus/{plusVersion} {osName}/{osVersion}. === Authentication === Most authentication uses OAuth 1.0. === Responses === Responses usually consist of a JSON (application/json) or binary plist (application/binary-plist) document with the root node being a dictionary, where most of the response data is stored. This dictionary always contains the key success, a '''true''' or '''false''' value which is true if the request was successful. When this page gives concrete examples, it assumes JSON is being used, but as long as the http Accept header contains the MIME type for binary plists they can be used too. === Error Responses === Error responses (that aren't completely fatal) still give HTTP status 200 OK (or 304 Not Modified when using ETags), but will have success set to false in the response body, an error field containing a numerical error code, and an error_msg string.https://web.archive.org/web/20100428132215im_/http://app.plusplus.com/users/update_passwordhttps://web.archive.org/web/20131120015720im_/http://app.mobage.com:80/1/Bahamut-Android/sessionhttps://web.archive.org/web/20150807000506im_/http://app.mobage.com:80/users/2903f0ce1bb30fa45713d75f0573b8c1a55625c6/opt_out For example: { "success": false, "error": 404, "error_msg": "Playername not found!" } === Common Data Types === ==== ''User'' ==== An object/dictionary containing info about a given user: * user_id (int): User ID * gamertag: Display name (gamername) * badge_id: The ID of the user's public profile image * photo_url: The user's friends-only profile photo URL * motto: Short status text, similar to a Discord status * email: Email address * email_hash: Hash of the email address * phone_number: Phone number * password: Hash of the user's password * first_name: First name * last_name: Last name * fullname_privacy (bool): Should the user's full name be private? * age_restricted (bool): Is this user age restricted? * new_buddy (bool): Is this user a new buddy relative to the currently logged in user? * mutual_friends (bool): Is this user a mutual relative to the logged in user? * capabilities: Object describing what the user is capable of: ** push_notifications (0 or 1): (Probably) Can this user can receive push notifiactions? * hide_presence (bool): Should this user's online status be hidden? * friend_only_notification (bool): Should this user only see notifications from friends? * lite (bool): Is this a lite user? * gamerscore (int): The user's gamer score * level_position (int): The user's level * level_name: Name of the level this user is at * level_points (int): Points the user has for the current level * level_next_points (int): Points (remaining/required?) for to the next level * games: Array of ''[[Plus+#Game|Game]]'' objects this user plays Many elements can be nil, especially if they are private to the user themselves. ==== ''Game'' ==== An object describing various information about a game, including it's identifier (key), screenshots (Mobage only), icon, description and a link to the store page for it. * app_key: Application identifier string (e.g. PetCat, PetDog2, RolandoTwoMTX) * name: App title displayed to the user * icon_url: App icon URL * publisher: Publisher name * catalog_url: Catalog URL (possibly the link to the game's page on the Plus+ website?) * feed_url: Feed URL (?) * app_store_url: App store URL * master_product_id: Master product ID (?) * featured (bool): If the app is featured or not * leaderboards_count (int): Number of leaderboards * achievements_count (int): Number of possible achievements ==== ''Score'' ==== A dictionary containing info about a score: *score: The score as a number *formatted_score: The score as displayed to the user * user_id: User the score applies to * gamertag: Gamer name of the user * badge_id: Badge ID of the user * rank: Position on the leaderboard (probably) === Routes === In no real order (also for now these are just the routes from ~2010 -- IIRC mobage has more than this): ==== PUT session ==== Set Apple Push Notification token * device_token: APN token Response is ignored, but should probably be {success: true}. ==== GET ping ==== Really simple request to ping the server. In touch pets, this happens after leaving the game open while the device falls asleep for a while, unsure if this is intended behaviour. ==== POST games/:appkey/leaderboards/:leaderboardIndex/scores ==== Submit a new high score (does not work for lite accounts) * level (int): Leaderboard index * score (int): Score to submit * gamertag (string): The player's gamername Response: * score ([[Plus+#Score|''Score'']]): The new score ==== GET games/:appkey/leaderboards ==== Get leaderboards for a game Query parameters: * user_id (optional): Show score for this user ID Response: * leaderboards: A list of objects describing each leaderboard: ** score ([[Plus+#Score|''Score'']]): (Presumably) The top score ** level (int): Leaderboard index ** title (string): Leaderboard title ** icon_url (string): Leaderboard icon URL ==== GET games/:appkey/leaderboards/:leaderboardIndex ==== Get scores for a leaderboard * relation (optional enum): Relationship relative to the logged in user; if present, this is friends * user_id (int): Current user's ID * count (int): Number of scores to retrieve * offset (int): Offset into the number of scores to retrieve, (probably) when ordered from best to worst Response: * leaderboard (list of [[Plus+#Score|''Score'']]): A list of scores in the leaderboard * title (string): (Probably) Name of the leaderboard * level (int): Leaderboard index * icon_url (string): Leaderboard icon URL * user_score ([[Plus+#Score|''Score'']]): The current user's score (may be optional) * offset (int): Offset into the leaderboard returned * total (int): Number of scores returned ==== GET users/:userId/achievements ==== Get achievements for this user * target_app_key (optional string): The app key of the game to fetch achievements for ==== POST invitations ==== Invite a user to join Plus+ directly via email * email: Email address ==== DELETE users/:userId/photo ==== ==== GET badges ==== Get the list of public profile icons. Response: * list: List of profile image sections: ** name (string): Name of the section ** badges: List of badges in section: *** id (int): badge ID *** icon_url (string): badge's icon URL ==== GET users/:userId/badges ==== Ditto, but probably also shows ones you've earned/unlocked (?) ==== GET session ==== Check session validity (also returns user's profile info). * id: This device's unique identifier * device_type: Type of device being used (e.g. iPhone) * os_version: Operating system and version in the form {osName}/{osVersion} * locale: The current language and region setting (e.g. en_GB) * timezone: Current user's time zone given by [[NSTimeZone defaultTimeZone] description] If successful, it responds with the following fields: * gamertag: The current gamertag of the user * badge_id: User's current badge ID * configuration: A dictionary containing the current Plus+ configuration (?) * messages: A list of dictionaries describing system messages ==== POST users/:userId/flags ==== User reporting * reason: Message with why the user was reported (formatted as [{gameTitle}][{location}]{message}) ==== GET users/:userId/buddies ==== Get relationships with other users * relation: Type of relationship * offset: Offset of relationships * count: Number of relationships to return ==== DELETE users/:userId/buddies/:relationshipid ==== Remove the relationship with another user ==== POST users/:userId/buddies ==== Create a new relationship * id: The ID of the user who the user wants to create a relationship with * enemy: The string "true" if this should be an enemy relationship or "false" if this is a friendship ==== GET users/:userId ==== Get profile information for a given user. Responds with a ''[[Plus+#User|User]]'' object. ==== DELETE session ==== Log out ==== POST users/update_social_photo ==== Update this user's social photo (exact purpose unknown) * social_type: Probably the type of social media ==== GET users/search ==== Search for users by user name or email address. There are two types of user search. The first is searching by gamername with the option for wildcards: * gamertag (string): Gamertag of the user to search for. This may include wildcards (*). * offset (int): Offset into the number of users * limit (int): Max number of users to return The other is searching by the SHA1 hash of the user's email address: * email_hash (string): The SHA-1 hash of the user's email converted to a hex string Both have a response of the form: * list (list of [[Plus+#User|Users]]): Users matching criteria * offset (int): Offset into the full result list * total (int): Total number of users returned ==== POST users ==== User registration ==== POST users/validate ==== Validate first name, last name, username, or email * field (string): Name of field to validate, one of gamertag, email, first_name or last_name * value (string): Value to validate The success of this request indicates if the value is valid. If it is, the response is a simple success response. For gamernames, the error response may contain a suggestions field which contains a list of suggested alternative names. ==== POST users/reset_password ==== Issue a password reset request * email: User's email address Returns a basic response (only has success field or error) ==== POST session ==== Login ==== PUT users/:userId ==== Update the user's information, possibly also updating their password * motto (string): The user's motto (similar to Discord status) * email (string): Email address * phone_number (string): Phone number * first_name (string): First name of the user * last_name (string): Last name of the user * fullname_privacy: If the user's full name should be hidden or not (0 or 1) * hide_presence: If the user's presence (online status) should be hidden or not (0 or 1) * friend_only_notification: Only show notifications from friends * badge_id (optional): Badge ID (public profile image) * password (optional string): Password, only present if changing password * password_confirmation (optional string): Password (again), only present if changing password ==== POST oauth/authorize_new ==== ==== POST users/:userId/photo ==== Upload new friends only profile photo * foo (string): always bar * photo (file): jpeg file with name photo.jpg ==== GET users/:userId/user_data ==== Get a list of all keys stored on the Plus+ server (for the iSave feature) Response: * datas (list of strings): List of keys present on the server ==== GET users/:userId/user_data/:key ==== Get data blob associated with a key. The Content-Type of the response should be application/octet-stream. ==== POST users/:userId/user_data ==== Set a data blob associated with a key * key (string): Name of the data blob/its key * privacy (int): Integer denoting if this value can be retrieved publicly, only by friends or only by the user themself (0 = private, 1 = friends, 2 = public) * value (file): Value of the data blob, as a file with the filename set to value ==== GET games/:appkey ==== ==== GET users/:userId/games ==== ==== GET games ==== ==== GET games/:appid/leaderboards ==== ==== GET challenges/:challengeId ==== ==== POST challenges ==== ==== GET challenges ==== ==== PUT challenges/:challengeId ==== ==== POST notifications ==== ==== PUT store_transactions/:transactionId ==== ==== GET store_transactions/:transactionId ==== ==== POST store_transactions ==== ==== GET user_offers ==== ==== PUT user_offers/:offerId ==== ==== POST social_accounts/search ==== ==== GET users/:userId/social_accounts/:accountId ==== ==== DELETE users/:userId/social_accounts/:accountId ==== ==== POST users/:userId/social_accounts ==== Create a social account ==== PUT users/:userId/social_accounts/:accountId ==== Update account ==== POST users/:userId/social_accounts/add_buddies ==== ==== GET user_updates ==== Fetch user status updates Response: * update_interval (float): Time in seconds to next update * online_friends (list of [[Plus+#user|''Users'']]): A list of the user's friends that are online * updates (list of dicts): A list of dictionaries containing record updates: ** record_id (int): Record ID ** key: Key ** data: Value == References ==
